description:
DECISION: The forbidden character test in is_valid_message_id() uses the closure |c: char| (c as u32) <= 0x20 || c == '<' || c == '>' || c as u32 == 0x7f rather than char::is_whitespace() or a regex. The bound <= 0x20 (not < 0x20) is intentional: it covers all C0 controls (0x00-0x1F) and space (0x20). NUL (0x00) is explicitly in scope. DEL (0x7F) is rejected by the separate c as u32 == 0x7f check.

WHY RIGHT: Rust's char::is_whitespace() returns false for '\0' (NUL), because Unicode does not classify NUL as whitespace. A NUL byte in a Message-ID used as a map key or in the canonical serialiser (which uses '\x00\n' as the header/body separator) would corrupt storage or produce an incorrect CID. The <= 0x20 formulation is both correct and self-documenting: the comment in the code spells out exactly why is_whitespace() alone is insufficient. DEL must also be rejected — it is not whitespace in Unicode but is a control character forbidden by RFC 5322 in structured header fields.

ALTERNATIVES REJECTED:
- char::is_whitespace(): misses NUL — the exact character that would corrupt the canonical byte stream.
- Regex: adds a dependency and is slower; the set of forbidden characters is small and fixed.
- Allowlist (only permit printable ASCII 33-126): would be stricter and more correct in theory, but international Message-IDs with non-ASCII local parts exist in practice. The denylist approach rejects the dangerous characters without breaking legitimate edge cases.
title: forbidden closure uses (c as u32) <= 0x20 to cover NUL and space; explicit DEL check
